result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter is about a visit to the vision rehabilitation office. You have a history of macular degeneration. You said you had photodynamic therapy (PDT, a light-activated treatment) in the last year.

Your small handheld magnifier helps you only a little.

The team found a mild change in your distance correction (the strength of your distance lenses). With the new distance correction, you could see 20/70 with your right eye. You could see 20/200 with your left eye.

With +4 reading glasses, you could read 0.5M print quite nicely.

The doctor thinks you are an excellent candidate for low vision help.

## What you need to do
1. Use the +4 reading glasses the doctor loaned you.
2. Keep doing the fine-detailed reading you started at the visit.
3. Come back to the office in two weeks.
4. At that visit, the doctor will decide which near reading glasses to prescribe for you.

## Dates and medicines
- Return visit: in two weeks, at the vision rehabilitation office.
- The date of your visit is not clear in the letter.
- Medicines: the letter lists no medicines.
- Loaned item: a pair of +4 reading glasses.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Do I need new distance glasses after the mild change?
- What does macular degeneration mean for my eyes?
- What will happen at my visit in two weeks?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
